chunks: And from him (Al-Hassan ibn Mahbub) from Al-Hassan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Abu Ubaydah al-Hadda' who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who vowed to walk to Mecca barefoot. He said: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) went out for Hajj and looked at a woman walking among the camels. He said: "Who is this?" They said: "The sister of Uqbah ibn Amir, who vowed to walk to Mecca barefoot." The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: "O Uqbah, go to your sister and tell her to ride, for Allah is Rich from her walking and her being barefoot." He said: "So she rode."'

And whoever Hajj becomes obligatory upon him but he is unable to rise for it due to old age or an illness that stands between him and it, or a matter for which Allah excuses him, then he should send someone to perform Hajj on his behalf, and that will suffice for him for the Hajj of Islam. What indicates this is what he narrated:
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for someone who vows to walk to Mecca barefoot or cannot perform Hajj due to old age or illness?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the principle of *raf' al-haraj* (removal of hardship) in Shia jurisprudence, where the Prophet’s command for Ummu Akhtham to ride demonstrates that voluntary vows are subject to the same ease granted in obligatory acts. It further establishes the validity of *hajj al-badal* (substitute Hajj) for those physically incapacitated, a ruling supported by the precedent of Zubayr ibn al-Awwam performing Hajj on behalf of the Prophet’s wife Salma bint Amr.
